beats.headline: Car wash owner buys Joe's farm
beats.body: The owner of the roadside car wash has bought old Joe's farm outside Willowbrook. The vegetables are ripe, the stand is open and the village is already queueing.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Pick what's ripe, fill the stand, and never keep a neighbour waiting. Everyone here knows everyone.

beats.headline: Sweet corn returns to Willowbrook
beats.body: For the first time in years there's corn growing on Joe's old farm. Villagers say it's the sweetest they've tasted.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Corn takes its time, but folk pay more for it. Keep both fields busy.

beats.headline: Fresh eggs on Joe's old farm
beats.body: Four hens have moved into a bright red hen house on the farm, and the first cartons of eggs are already on the stand. Villagers are stopping by just for them.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Collect them while they're warm and pack them six to a carton. Happy hens, happy customers.

beats.headline: Farm stand hires a helper
beats.body: There's now a friendly face behind the farm stand all day, so the owner can spend more time in the fields.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Now you're farming like an owner. Let your helper sell; you keep the crates coming.

beats.headline: A farmhand joins the crew
beats.body: The farm's new hand picks the fields and carries the crates to the stand. The village has never seen the place so busy.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Good help is worth every penny. The farm runs itself while you plan what's next.

beats.headline: A new red barn on Joe's farm
beats.body: The farm's big red barn is open, storing crates by the dozen. Shoppers say the produce has never been fresher.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: I always dreamed of a barn like that. You did it proper.

beats.headline: Willowbrook animals go corn-fed
beats.body: The farm's new feed store turns its own corn into feed. Corn-fed hens lay twice as fast, the cows give more milk, and the stand can hardly keep up.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Every crate of corn in that hopper comes back as eggs and milk. Keep it topped up and the animals will do the rest.

beats.headline: Willowbrook Farm puts up its sign
beats.body: A painted sign now hangs over the farm gate, and folk from the next valley are driving over for the eggs, the milk and the produce.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: A good sign brings folk from miles around. Now feed those animals proper and they'll give you twice as much.

beats.headline: Cows come home to Willowbrook
beats.body: A cow has moved into a brand-new cow barn on the farm (with room for two more), and fresh milk is on sale in the village for the first time in years.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Milk them gently and bottle it cold. Nothing sells like fresh milk.

beats.headline: Goldsby Agri moves into the valley
beats.body: Rex Goldsby, the chain owner beaten in the car wash war, is back. His company Goldsby Agri is buying up farms and selling cheap to the village, and fewer shoppers are stopping at the farm stand.
beats.speaker: rival
beats.words: Deliveries? Cute. My trucks are bigger.

beats.headline: Goldsby Agri pulls out of Willowbrook
beats.body: With its own milk tanker on the road, the farm now delivers fresher milk than anyone. Goldsby Agri has sold its farms and left the valley. Talk is of an orchard next.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Better service beats a bigger truck. Now, a few apple trees down by the lane would do nicely...

beats.headline: Heatwave dries out the valley
beats.body: The hottest week in years has dried up gardens all over Willowbrook. For the next three minutes villagers will pay double for anything fresh.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: When the gardens dry up, folk come to us. Keep that stand full!

beats.headline: Rain at last for Willowbrook
beats.body: The heatwave has broken and the fields are green again. While the valley was parched, Joe's old farm kept everyone fed, and the next harvest is already coming in.

beats.headline: Apple trees planted on Joe's farm
beats.body: Six apple trees now stand in a row down by the farm lane. Once their blossom sets they fruit again and again, and the village is already asking about apple pies.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Trees are patient business. Plant them, wait, and they pay you every year after.

beats.headline: Willowbrook has a bakery again
beats.body: The farm's new mill and bakery turns its own corn into warm bread, and its apples into pies. Bread sells for twice what the corn did.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Corn is cheap, bread is not. Every step you add to a crate is money in your pocket.

beats.headline: Farmers' market draws weekend crowds
beats.body: Striped stalls by the road, fresh food and music: the farm's new market brings shoppers from all over the valley, and they pay top prices.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: People come for the food and stay for the fun. Keep those stalls full!

beats.headline: A windmill turns over Willowbrook again
beats.body: Thirty years after the last one came down, a new windmill stands on the farm's west paddock, its sails turning. The village fair was held under it, and every shop in the valley is busier for it. Talk is turning to the old Starlight fairground across town, closed these twenty years.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: You've made this valley proud. Mabel rode the carousel at the old Starlight fairground as a girl. It's been closed twenty years. The land's for sale, if you can raise the money.
